jurisdiction.name: Azerbaijan
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Azerbaijan governs AI through its first national AI Strategy for 2025-2028, approved by presidential order in March 2025, coordinated by the Cabinet of Ministers and led by the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport, with a 2025 cabinet implementation order, a 2026 list of national priority sectors for AI and a presidential Action Plan for 2026-2028 on accelerating digital development whose AI priority covers a national high-performance computing centre, an AI index for state bodies, Azerbaijani-language language models and a regulatory test environment. Two 2026 laws amend the Criminal Code: one makes non-consensual AI-generated content a criminal offence and requires labelling of AI-generated content, the other extends the sabotage article to acts using AI technologies; the 2010 personal data law applies. The national standards body has adopted the ISO/IEC AI risk-management and data life-cycle standards. Cabinet rules on AI ethics, AI and personal data, an AI regulatory sandbox and high-performance computing were still drafts in October 2026.
lead_institutions: President of the Republic of Azerbaijan
Ministry of Digital Development and Transport
narrative.review_notes: The review of 12 October 2026, updated on 22 October 2026, covers national law, the President's and Cabinet's acts, ministries, the standards institute and regulators; the national legal database and the central bank's library were not opened directly. Several draft cabinet rules on AI, a standalone AI draft law and the ISO/IEC 42001 adoption are listed as leads.

instruments.current_status: Approved by Presidential Order No. 530 of 19 March 2025 (order number as cited in the Cabinet of Ministers' implementing order of 28 April 2025). It is the current national AI strategy (no earlier stand-alone AI strategy found). The president.az page carries the order; the full strategy and action plan are published by the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport (listed on its legislation page dated 01.04.2025). The Ministry reported in October 2026 that implementing Cabinet rules are still in draft (see leads).
instruments.summary: Presidential order approving Azerbaijan's first national AI strategy for 2025-2028, with sections on global trends, current situation, target indicators, goals, priority directions, financing and an action plan. The order makes the Cabinet of Ministers responsible for coordinating and overseeing implementation and reporting annually to the President, tasks the Special Communication and Information Security State Service with analysing information-security risks of AI used in state bodies, and assigns monitoring to the Center for Analysis of Economic Reforms and Communication. The action plan provides for designating priority sectors and responsible bodies, a normative framework for responsible and ethical AI, rules on personal-data protection in AI systems, AI standardisation, data infrastructure, an AI Academy and skills measures.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy and the legal basis for Azerbaijan's AI governance measures.

instruments.current_status: Law No. 387-VIIQD signed 21 April 2026; the text does not state an entry-into-force date. Law 449-VIIQD cites the Media Law as amended by it.
instruments.summary: Amending law adding Criminal Code Article 148-2 (making or disseminating, without consent, AI- or special-software-generated photo, video or audio that does not reflect reality using a person's image or voice; fines of 3,000-7,000 manat up to three years' imprisonment, three to five years if aggravated) and Article 242-1 (non-consensual AI-generated pornographic or sexual content; three to seven years). It amends the Law on Information, Informatization and Protection of Information to classify such material as prohibited and to require that AI-generated photo, video or audio material shown publicly carries a clear, easily visible label, and amends the Media Law to bar media from disseminating such material.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First Azerbaijani statute with AI-specific offences and a labelling obligation for AI-generated content.

instruments.summary: General personal data law governing the collection, processing and protection of personal data, the personal-data segment of the national information space and cross-border transfers, and setting the rights and duties of state bodies, municipalities and legal and natural persons. It applies to personal data used to train and operate AI systems; it has no AI-specific or automated-decision provisions.

instruments.english_title: Order of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan approving the Action Plan for 2026–2028 on accelerating digital development in the Republic of Azerbaijan (27 February 2026)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Azerbaijan
instruments.publisher_name: President of the Republic of Azerbaijan
instruments.current_status: Order signed in Baku on 27 February 2026; the copy read is the full text with the annexed Action Plan published by the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport (the order's number is not printed in that copy). The order sets no separate entry-into-force date.
instruments.summary: Presidential order approving the 2026–2028 Action Plan to accelerate digital development, financed from the state budget, coordinated by the Digital Development Council with quarterly reporting by the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport and monitoring by the Economic Reforms Analysis and Communication Center. Priority direction 6.1.3 is devoted to AI technologies: state support mechanisms for AI adoption, a national GPU-based high-performance computing centre with quota access for start-ups and researchers, AI performance indicators and an AI index in each state body's annual plan, Azerbaijani-language large language models and AI virtual assistants for public services, stronger personal-data protection where AI systems are used, a regulatory test environment (sandbox) for AI and innovative digital solutions, and a staged legal framework for autonomous vehicles. Other items require AI roadmaps with key performance indicators in state bodies, AI-based public services, AI detection of prohibited online content, and a deputy-level official for digitalisation, innovation, AI and cyber security in every state body.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Government action plan that sets the public-sector AI governance measures (AI index, AI roadmaps, AI officials, sandbox, data protection in AI) for 2026–2028.

instruments.issuing_authority: Milli Majlis of the Republic of Azerbaijan (signed by the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan)
instruments.publisher_name: Milli Majlis of the Republic of Azerbaijan
instruments.current_status: Law No. 395-VIIQD signed in Baku on 27 April 2026; the text states no entry-into-force date.
instruments.summary: Amending law that redrafts Criminal Code Article 282 (sabotage) so that it covers acts aimed at weakening Azerbaijan's defence capability, economic security or scientific-technical potential by destroying, damaging or disrupting life-support and critical information infrastructure, energy, transport and telecommunications networks, including acts committed for that purpose using artificial intelligence technologies or special software, with aggravated forms for organised groups, emergencies or martial law, officials and negligent death. It also adds Article 214-4 on creating, leading or taking part in a terrorist organisation and amends the Law on Combating Terrorism accordingly.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General criminal law with an explicit AI provision: the use of AI technologies as a means of sabotage against critical infrastructure.

instruments.english_title: AZS ISO/IEC 23894:2024 Information technology – Artificial intelligence – Guidance on risk management (Azerbaijani national standard)
instruments.current_status: First edition, designated AZS ISO/IEC 23894:2024, identical to ISO/IEC 23894:2023; the preface on the Institute's site leaves the approval date and decision number blank.
instruments.summary: Azerbaijani national standard adopting ISO/IEC 23894:2023 in Azerbaijani, giving guidance on managing the risks of products, systems and services that use AI. It applies the ISO 31000 risk-management process to AI, describes AI-specific risk sources and objectives, and refers normatively to the Azerbaijani adoption of ISO/IEC 22989 (AI concepts and terminology).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National standards body adoption of the international AI risk-management standard, usable as a voluntary assurance reference by Azerbaijani organisations.

instruments.english_title: AZS ISO/IEC 8183:2024 Information technology – Artificial intelligence – Data life cycle framework (Azerbaijani national standard)
instruments.current_status: First edition, designated AZS ISO/IEC 8183:2024, identical to ISO/IEC 8183:2023; the preface on the Institute's site leaves the approval date and decision number blank.
instruments.summary: Azerbaijani national standard adopting ISO/IEC 8183:2023 in Azerbaijani, which defines the stages and actions of the data life cycle for developing and using AI systems, from idea origination and requirements through data acquisition, data preparation, model building, deployment and operation to data and system decommissioning. It gives organisations a common framework for data processing in AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National standards body adoption of the international AI data life-cycle standard.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. e-qanun.az full-text search is JavaScript-only (laws read on meclis.gov.az and the ministry's pages). AZSTAND catalogue and cbar.az library not reached. Decision 226 PDF omits the annexed sector list; Law 387-VIIQD has no stated entry-into-force date. Convention 108: Law No. 879-IIIQ of 30 September 2009, recorded on the COE file. Units covered: Law: meclis.gov.az: Law 387-VIIQD (21 Apr 2026) AI deepfake offences + labelling read; Law on Personal Data (2010) read via MDDT legislation page; standalone AI bill only reported (lead). e-qanun.az not searchable by curl (SPA) - laws read on meclis.gov.az / ministry pages instead.; Government: president.az order on AI Strategy 2025-2028 + full strategy (mincom PDF); Cabinet (nk.gov.az) implementing order 253s (28 Apr 2025) and decision 226 (21 Jul 2026) read. No earlier stand-alone AI strategy found.; Ministries: Ministry of Digital Development and Transport: legislation pages and site search reviewed; 8 Oct 2026 news lists four draft Cabinet acts (ethics requirements, AI & personal data rules, HPC requirements, regulatory test environment) - leads. Education, health, justice, defence, finance, labour, interior: searched via discovery queries, no AI-specific published documents found.; Regulators: Central Bank (cbar.az): AI frameworks announced but none published (lead). Personal data: no separate DPA, no AI guidance. Cyber: Special Communication and Information Security State Service tasked by the strategy order, no published AI security guidance found. AZSTAND ISO/IEC 42001 adoption reported only (lead). Competition/media regulators: nothing AI-specific found.. Not reached: e-qanun.az full-text search (JavaScript application; not queried directly); AZSTAND standards catalogue; cbar.az document library (only discovery searches). leads.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Azerbaijan
leads.note: Approved by presidential order of 10 December 2025 (full text on static.president.az). 2026-10-22: strategy text read; AI appears in measures 6.1.1.2.3, 6.1.4.2.2 and 6.1.9.1 and as key initiative 6.2.5 (an Azerbaijani-language AI model for the Ministry of Economy), with no dedicated AI priority direction; kept out of the records as a general digital strategy. leads.title: “Azərbaycan Respublikasında rəqəmsal inkişafın sürətləndirilməsinə dair 2026−2028-ci illər üçün Fəaliyyət Planı”nın təsdiq edilməsi haqqında Prezidentin Sərəncamı (27 fevral 2026)
leads.note: Presidential order dated 27 February 2026 on president.az approving the Digital Development Acceleration Action Plan 2026-2028; the plan itself is an attachment not shown on the page. Ministry news (https://mincom.gov.az/en/media-en/news/digital-development-acceleration-action-plan-for-2026-2028-approved-what-to-expect, 2 March 2026) says it includes a legal framework for national roll-out of AI solutions tested in the regulatory sandbox, AI-based public services, HPC infrastructure, and a deputy-level AI official in each government body. Add as strategy once the plan annex (static.president.az PDF) is read and the AI measures confirmed.
